raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Fix https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58599, https://github.com/pytorch/test-infra/issues/8931

### What's wrong

The MiniMax fused allreduce+RMSNorm kernel needs each GPU to read the other GPUs' memory directly. To set that up, every GPU allocates a buffer, gets a small 64-byte "IPC handle" for it, and sends that handle to the other GPUs. They then use it to open the buffer.

vLLM converted the handle to bytes and back through its .reserved field. In cuda-bindings 13.4 (part of cuda-python), NVIDIA removed that field from cudaIpcMemHandle_t, so the code now fails with:
AttributeError: 'cuda.bindings.runtime.cudaIpcMemHandle_t' object has no attribute 'reserved'


When that happens, vLLM falls back to the slower non-fused path, and test_minimax_reduce_rms_qk fails. It shows up in the torch-nightly CI lane because that environment installs cuda-bindings 13.4.x.

### The fix

Copy the 64 handle bytes through handle.getPtr(), the handle's memory address, using ctypes. Every cuda-bindings version supports it, so no version check is needed.

_ipc_handle_to_bytes(handle) reads the 64 bytes out of a handle.
_ipc_handle_from_bytes(raw) creates a new handle and copies the 64 bytes into it.
The fix is limited to vllm/model_executor/layers/minimax_rms_norm/lamport_workspace.py.


### Test plan
pytest tests/kernels/core/test_minimax_reduce_rms.py::test_minimax_reduce_rms_qk -k "2-"
Before: fails with the AttributeError above and logs "Falling back to the eager allreduce".
After: 6 passed, 12 skipped (the 4- and 8-GPU cases, since there are only 2 GPUs). The fallback message is gone, so the fused path runs.

detail.title: [Fix] MiniMax: fix CUDA IPC handle exchange on cuda-bindings >= 13.4

files.patch:
@@ -4,6 +4,7 @@
 
 import array
 import contextlib
+import ctypes
 import struct
 import sys
 import threading
@@ -16,6 +17,7 @@
     from cuda import cudart
 
 _ALIGN = 1 << 21  # 2 MiB — CUDA IPC allocation alignment
+_IPC_HANDLE_SIZE = 64  # sizeof(cudaIpcMemHandle_t)
 
 
 # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
@@ -30,6 +32,20 @@ def _check(error):
         raise RuntimeError(f"CUDA runtime error: {error}")
 
 
+# cuda-bindings >= 13.4 no longer exposes cudaIpcMemHandle_t.reserved, so
+# copy the raw handle bytes through getPtr() instead. This is safe because the
+# CUDA ABI fixes the handle as an opaque 64-byte struct (char reserved[64]).
+def _ipc_handle_to_bytes(handle) -> bytes:
+    return ctypes.string_at(handle.getPtr(), _IPC_HANDLE_SIZE)
+
+
+def _ipc_handle_from_bytes(raw: bytes):
+    assert len(raw) == _IPC_HANDLE_SIZE, len(raw)
+    handle = cudart.cudaIpcMemHandle_t()
+    ctypes.memmove(handle.getPtr(), raw, _IPC_HANDLE_SIZE)
+    return handle
+
+
 def _cuda_malloc(size: int):
     aligned = ((size + _ALIGN - 1) >> 21) << 21
     err, ptr = cudart.cudaMalloc(aligned)
@@ -84,15 +100,16 @@ def __init__(self, rank: int, world_size: int, size: int, process_group=None):
 
         all_handles: list[bytes | None] = [None] * world_size
         torch.distributed.all_gather_object(
-            all_handles, bytes(local_handle.reserved), group=process_group
+            all_handles, _ipc_handle_to_bytes(local_handle), group=process_group
         )
 
         for r in range(world_size):
             if r == rank:
                 self.peer_ptrs[r] = self.local_ptr
             else:
-                handle = cudart.cudaIpcMemHandle_t()
-                handle.reserved = all_handles[r]
+                raw = all_handles[r]
+                assert raw is not None
+                handle = _ipc_handle_from_bytes(raw)
                 err, ptr = cudart.cudaIpcOpenMemHandle(
                     handle, cudart.cudaIpcMemLazyEnablePeerAccess
                 )
